Classical.inhabited_of_nonempty.code: Classical.inhabited_of_nonempty.{u} {α : Sort u} (h : Nonempty α) : Inhabited α
Classical.inhabited_of_nonempty.fullDefinition: noncomputable def inhabited_of_nonempty {α : Sort u} (h : Nonempty α) : Inhabited α :=   ⟨choice h⟩
Classical.inhabited_of_nonempty.description: A non-empty type implies that there exists at least one element of that type.

Classical.choose.code: Classical.choose.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ x, p x) : α
Classical.choose.comment:
Given that there exists an element satisfying `p`, returns one such element.

This is a straightforward consequence of, and equivalent to, `Classical.choice`.

See also `choose_spec`, which asserts that the returned value has property `p`.
Classical.choose.fullDefinition: noncomputable def choose {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ x, p x) : α :=   (indefiniteDescription p h).val
Classical.choose.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.

Classical.not_not.comment:
The Double Negation Theorem: `¬¬P` is equivalent to `P`.
The left-to-right direction, double negation elimination (DNE),
is classically true but not constructively.
Classical.not_not.description: The Double Negation Theorem states that the negation of the negation of a proposition is equivalent to the proposition itself.

Classical.or_iff_not_imp_left.code: Classical.or_iff_not_imp_left {a b : Prop} : a ∨ b ↔ ¬a → b
Classical.or_iff_not_imp_left.description: The statement asserts that the disjunction of two propositions is equivalent to the implication that if the first is false, then the second must be true.

Classical.choose_spec.code: Classical.choose_spec.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ x, p x) : p (Classical.choose h)
Classical.choose_spec.description: Selecting an element that satisfies a property guarantees that this element indeed possesses that property.

Classical.indefiniteDescription.code: Classical.indefiniteDescription.{u} {α : Sort u} (p : α → Prop) (h : ∃ x, p x) : { x // p x }
Classical.indefiniteDescription.fullDefinition: noncomputable def indefiniteDescription {α : Sort u} (p : α → Prop) (h : ∃ x, p x) : {x // p x} :=   choice <| let ⟨x, px⟩ := h; ⟨⟨x, px⟩⟩
Classical.indefiniteDescription.description: The existence of an element satisfying a given property ensures the ability to construct a type that contains precisely those elements fulfilling that property.

Exists.choose_spec.code: Exists.choose_spec.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} (P : ∃ a, p a) : p P.choose
Exists.choose_spec.comment: Show that an element extracted from `P : ∃ a, p a` using `P.choose` satisfies `p`.
Exists.choose_spec.description: An element chosen from an existence assertion satisfies the property asserted by that existence statement.

Classical.epsilon.code: Classical.epsilon.{u} {α : Sort u} [h : Nonempty α] (p : α → Prop) : α
Classical.epsilon.fullDefinition: noncomputable def epsilon {α : Sort u} [h : Nonempty α] (p : α → Prop) : α :=   (strongIndefiniteDescription p h).val
Classical.epsilon.description: The Hilbert epsilon function selects an element from a non-empty set that satisfies a given property.

Exists.choose.code: Exists.choose.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} (P : ∃ a, p a) : α
Exists.choose.comment: Extract an element from a existential statement, using `Classical.choose`.
Exists.choose.fullDefinition: @[reducible] noncomputable def Exists.choose {p : α → Prop} (P : ∃ a, p a) : α := Classical.choose P
Exists.choose.description: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.

Classical.em.comment: **Diaconescu's theorem**: excluded middle from choice, Function extensionality and propositional extensionality.
Classical.em.description: Every proposition is either true or false, a principle known as the law of excluded middle.

Classical.not_forall.code: Classical.not_forall.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} : (¬∀ (x : α), p x) ↔ ∃ x, ¬p x
Classical.not_forall.description: The equivalence between the negation of a universal statement and the existence of a counterexample is demonstrated by showing that not all elements satisfy the property if at least one element does not.

Classical.not_exists_not.code: Classical.not_exists_not.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {p : α → Prop} : (¬∃ x, ¬p x) ↔ ∀ (x : α), p x
Classical.not_exists_not.description: The absence of an element that does not satisfy a property is equivalent to the assertion that every element satisfies that property.

Classical.propDecidable.fullDefinition: noncomputable scoped instance (priority := low) propDecidable (a : Prop) : Decidable a :=   choice <| match em a with     | Or.inl h => ⟨isTrue h⟩     | Or.inr h => ⟨isFalse h⟩
Classical.propDecidable.description: Every proposition is determined to be either true or false, establishing its decidability.
